clue.text: New Avengers agent, lethal

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the following letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as printed

explanation.surface: A spy from the old television series The New Avengers is a deadly operative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Avengers' reads as the TV show's title, but 'New' is the instruction and the comma splits off a definition read backwards: a lethal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon, the kind of deadly chemical substance described as a lethal agent.

clue.text: Perhaps lacking sleep, second son leaves city

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so one letter drops out of the longer word

blocks.note: without a nap; 'Perhaps' admits the coinage is playful
S is the abbreviation for son; the second of the two in the word goes

explanation.surface: An insomniac's younger boy moves away from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPLESS has two S's together, so removing either gives the same result; 'second' just tells you which one the setter means.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large port in southern Italy, one example of the general category of urban settlement.

clue.text: Artist on generally gloomy film

blocks.note: RE means 'on the subject of', as in a letter heading
film noir is the genre of dark, gloomy crime films

explanation.surface: A painter appears in a broadly bleak movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generally' signals a genre rather than one film: noir is the whole class of dark thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter, so he is an instance of a painter.

clue.text: Rate changed to accommodate ten more

indicators.note: what is changed is altered, so the letters are put in a different order
to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece is housed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A charge was revised to fit ten additional guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters of the rate open up after their first letter to take in the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adjective or adverb means additional, in addition to what is usual.

clue.text: Fool an RAF commander?

blocks.note: first meaning: a silly, empty-headed person
second meaning, read literally: the head of the air force

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: someone in charge of the air could be called its head. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a stupid or scatterbrained person, someone with nothing between the ears.

clue.text: What acne treatments claim to do for tyrant

definitions.text: What acne treatments claim to do

blocks.clueFragment: What acne treatments claim to do
blocks.note: first meaning: to remove pimples
second meaning: an absolute ruler

explanation.surface: Skin creams promise results for a cruel dictator, of all people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two parts, DE (remove) plus SPOT, and it is what a spot cream advertises.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with total power who uses it cruelly, the same as a tyrant or dictator.

clue.text: Like Lassie, last of two animals put first?

indicators.note: the final letter of the whole string is the one picked out to move
placing something first sends it to the front, so the end letter jumps ahead

blocks.note: a pony and a mouse, side by side

explanation.surface: A question about Lassie the dog: the final one of a pair of creatures goes to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the film named after its canine star, so the title character is eponymous; move the end E of the animals to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Eponymous describes the character a work is named after, as the collie gives her name to the film.

clue.text: Where chemist works fast to dress wound

indicators.note: dressing something covers it all round, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: pacy means quick
to wound is to harm

explanation.surface: A druggist hurries to bandage an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress a wound' is first-aid language, but here 'wound' is a verb meaning injure and the dressing is done by the word for quick. In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is the shop or dispensary where a pharmacist prepares and sells medicines.

clue.text: Complication involving Rhode Island figure

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a tangle is a muddle or complication
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A snag involving a well-known person from Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' reads as a person in the story, but it is the geometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided plane shape, and in geometry any such shape is called a figure.

clue.text: One French court sitting in modest flat

indicators.note: whatever sits in something is placed inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: pure in the sense of chaste, virtuous
un is French for one
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A French judge lives in a humble apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, matching 'modest', but it is a flat tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, short for flat tyre, is a tyre that has lost its air, which a puncture causes; the two words are used interchangeably.

clue.text: African‘s some boxer with no English

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
Muhammad Ali, the most famous boxer
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A certain African fighter does not speak English.
explanation.walkthrough: The E dropped is the one at the end of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a person from Somalia, a country in the Horn of Africa, so an African.

clue.text: Resistance units sent for King Charles?

blocks.note: first meaning: measures of electrical resistance
second meaning: the initials printed on official mail, On His Majesty's Service

explanation.surface: Members of a rebel movement were dispatched on behalf of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: British government post is franked with the initials of On His Majesty's Service, and with Charles on the throne it is His, not Her.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, so several of them are resistance units.

clue.text: American in The Ritz: all obey volatile film star

indicators.note: to be in something is to be placed inside it
volatile means unstable and explosive, so the letters will not stay in their order

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A temperamental screen idol is staying at the famous London hotel, and every staff member jumps to her orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz is a grand London hotel. All fourteen letters of the phrase plus the A are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Taylor was a Hollywood actress, star of Cleopatra and many other movies, so a screen celebrity.

clue.text: Minions abandoning southern nation

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: yes-men are toadying followers
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Followers desert a country in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern nation' wants to be read together as the definition; 'southern' is the letter that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country at the south of the Arabian peninsula, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Elderly fumed? Not at first

indicators.note: telling us not to have the opening means the initial letter is dropped

blocks.note: to fume is to rage

explanation.surface: Was the old person angry? Not to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fumed' is a past-tense verb for losing one's temper; drop its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged as an adjective describes someone old, advanced in years, just as elderly does.

clue.text: Wife never climbing in pleasant forest

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters read in the opposite direction
being in something places it inside the outer word

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
good means nice, pleasant

explanation.surface: A wife refuses to scale trees in a pleasant wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Wife and the poetic never are joined first and the pair is turned over as a unit before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwood is a literary word for a forest in leaf, the home of Robin Hood and his outlaws.

clue.text: Job so described in Costa I stupidly left

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A boring job is described as stupid by someone who quit Costa, the British coffee chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is not employment but the Biblical Job, famed for enduring suffering patiently; the capital letter is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Job shows him bearing every disaster without complaint, which is exactly what stoical means: enduring hardship calmly.

clue.text: Servant saving 50 leads cheers in capital city

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece is held within another
what leads goes in front, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a valet is a manservant
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A servant rescuing fifty people heads the celebrations in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is British for thank you as well as applause, and its short informal form is TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital of Malta, the seat of its government, so a capital city.

clue.text: Much obliged to a hunky criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grateful response to a good-looking lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' sits at the end as a noun in the surface but works as an adjective on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Much obliged is a formal phrase of gratitude, said in exactly the same situations as this expression.

clue.text: Reach that is very limited by pain

indicators.note: something limited by another is bounded on both sides by it

blocks.note: an ache is a pain
i.e. abbreviates the Latin for 'that is'
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A stretch that is severely restricted by an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces are joined and slipped in before the last letter of the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a goal is to attain or accomplish it, the transitive sense of achieve.

clue.text: French are binding feet for amphibians

indicators.note: to bind something is to wrap round it, so the outer letters enclose the inner

blocks.note: es is French for 'are' as in 'tu es'
FT is the abbreviation for feet

explanation.surface: The French tie up their feet to make frogs and toads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French are' means the French verb form, not the people.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is an old or dialect name for a newt, and newts are amphibians.

clue.text: Dog-sledder’s forwarding address in grim US hamlet

indicators.note: being in a phrase means the letters are found inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A sled-dog driver's postal address is in a bleak American village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forwarding address' sounds like mail, but it means the word addressed to the dogs to send them forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Mush is the command a musher shouts to a team of sled dogs to make them move forward.

clue.text: Mrs Bale lost sanity

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Mrs Bale went out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the idiom 'lost her marbles', which is exactly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbles is informal for one's wits, as in the idiom about losing them meaning going mad.

clue.text: Time to stop that chap, an assassin

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so this letter fills the middle of the other word

blocks.note: him refers to a man already mentioned
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to halt that man, a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter plugs the gap between the second and third letters of the pronoun, then the article follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is someone paid to murder, a professional killer like an assassin.

clue.text: Echo in valley for dragon-slayer

indicators.note: being in something means it is placed inside

blocks.note: a gorge is a steep, narrow valley
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shout comes back from a valley for the hero who fought the dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' sounds like a valley's reverberation, but it is the radio code word for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George, patron saint of England, is the legendary knight who killed a dragon.

clue.text: See 28
Mistake is admitted by the heartless bully

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is taken away
what is admitted is let in, so it goes inside the outer word

blocks.note: the word with its middle letter removed
an error is a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel bully confesses to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless bully' wants to be read together as a picture of cruelty; 'heartless' applies to 'the' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, and to terrorise them is to fill them with fear by threats.

clue.text: Ruling class

blocks.note: first meaning: a decree or command issued by an authority
second meaning: a rank or category

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest the aristocracy, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order is an official ruling, and an order is also a social rank or a taxonomic category.

clue.text: See 12
Bolshevik leader‘s mandrill I’ve trained at home

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are drilled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A Russian revolutionary's pet monkey has been taught tricks in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: A mandrill is a large baboon. The 'at home' letters are added to the mix before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik party to power in the 1917 Russian Revolution and founded the Soviet state.

clue.text: Trouble drinking spirit in one strange situation

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the outer word swallows the inner

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone gets into trouble drinking liquor while stuck in an odd predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition stands for the article at the start. Rum is British slang for odd, and a do is an affair or event.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a rum do is a peculiar business or odd turn of events, so one strange situation.

clue.text: Separate book top class doesn’t need

indicators.note: what is not needed can be left out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: best means top, finest
B is the abbreviation for book
a range is a class or category of products

explanation.surface: A distinct textbook that the best pupils can do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top class' wants to be one phrase for an elite set, but the two words split: the first loses its book letter and the second is a category.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to alienate them or drive them apart, the verb sense of separating them.
